messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident 1769001123 detected — significant error spike and OOMs on inference nodes serving the 'llama2' model family. Auto-mitigation applied (soft throttle). Paging current on-call (alex). More info: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1769001123

alex: Saw the alert. Looking at graphs now — token error rate up ~8x, tail latency climbing. Which model variants are the worst?

maya: llama2-medium and llama2-large much higher CPU/GPU mem pressure. Most of the traffic is from anonymous hosted API requests hitting medium with long context.

jamal: Are enterprise customers affected or only public API? Need to decide if we drop global TPM or selectively throttle.

alex: Quick impact summary from logs: 12 customers saw >=5% error increase. Top 3 by requests: AcmeCorp, Datapulse, FinStream. No production-wide SLA breach yet but trend is fast.

maya: Suggest immediate per-model TPM drops for medium/large to reduce KV cache pressure and keep latency SLOs. Keep small untouched. Proposed: medium tpm -> 60 (from 450), large tpm -> 30 (from 200). RPM scaled accordingly.

jamal: For enterprise/dedicated customers we should exempt unless they requested dedicated capacity. We can add an allowlist for committed projects to avoid breaking them.

priya: I can run the quota change. We need a short maintenance note and then run commands. Will also add traffic-shape rule to slow down long-context requests.

alex: Ok run it. Priya, please apply throttles and post the commands/output here. I'll start customer outreach for the three most affected. @support-lead can you prepare a short status blurb?

support-lead: On it. Drafting: "We are throttling specific model variants to stabilize performance. If you're impacted, contact support with request ID."

priya: Running command now:
```
redwoodctl quota update --model llama2-medium --tpm 60 --rpm 300 --reason "live mitigation 1769001123"
redwoodctl quota update --model llama2-large --tpm 30 --rpm 180 --reason "live mitigation 1769001123"
redwoodctl traffic-shape add --match "model:llama2* AND context_tokens>4096" --delay 250ms
```

deploy-bot: Command output:
```
2026-03-15T16:05:12Z INFO quota updated llama2-medium tpm=60 rpm=300
2026-03-15T16:05:14Z INFO quota updated llama2-large tpm=30 rpm=180
2026-03-15T16:05:16Z INFO traffic-shape rule added id=ts-87 delay=250ms match=model:llama2* AND context_tokens>4096
```

maya: Seeing immediate drop in evicted KV cache churn, tail latency improving within ~30s. Error rate down ~60% on the worst nodes. Nice work.

jamal: Good. We should also enable fallback to quantized variants for long requests if we see sustained pressure. Add as next step.

alex: Agreed. For now keeping throttles in place. Priya leave a note in the runbook and reference this thread. I'll start a handoff to elena in 5m and include next steps: monitor latency, watch for customer escalations, prepare rollback plan.

elena: Taking handoff early. I'll monitor next 30m and coordinate with support if any customers escalate. If error rate creeps back up, we can further reduce TPM or temporarily disable non-priority features (structured output).

support-lead: Notified the three affected customers via support channel with the draft. Tracking responses.

alex: Final notes before handoff: 1) mitigation applied (per-model TPM reduced for medium/large) 2) traffic-shape rule in place for long-context requests 3) allowlisted enterprise customers unchanged 4) escalation path: page eng-sre if errors >10% baseline or tail latency >2s for 5 consecutive minutes.

elena: Copy. Handoff accepted. I'll update status page if we need to extend throttles beyond 2 hours.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: alex -> elena at 1769001450. Incident mitigated enough to stabilize service; monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:
